Ok so, games where you forget completely what your objective was supposed to be due to getting distracted with its own gameplay and just roaming around are absolutely awesome. Dying Light AKA the Vertigo Simulator just so happens to be one of them. You can completely ignore quests and instead go apeshit, killing every zombie in the open world, much like I myself did before doing the quests! I suggest completing them however, to start leveling up and making combat that much cooler. I keep laughing my ass off when I climb high buildings, then grapple the zombies and throw them off. I then watch them fly!

Where Dying Light shines, is definitely on the gameplay. It has the perfect recipe: responsive parkour movement, and zombies. The cherry on top is the punchy feeling of melee combat. Crane feels very nimble as we control him. And I have to mention how well optimized this game is, despite the graphics being pretty high quality!

The story is where it drops the ball. I wouldn't say it sucks exactly, since you do feel motivated and truly understand Crane's feelings and actions. Things are justified, and the environmental lore is not too bad either. Harran feels very much alive, like there used to be an actual thriving city before chaos struck. However, it's nothing to write home about, in essence. It's your average Far Cry-esque plot, with a villain, people you're supposed to root for, a reason is given to hate this and that character, etc. Everything is there, but it's not incredibly well written.

The Following DLC manages to have an even worse story than the base game, with poorly written characters, and nobody's personality is expanded on. The whole plot could be summed up to two or three sentences. Again, the gameplay is to be celebrated here: despite parkour being one of the selling points of Dying Light, The Following cuts down on it and instead has us explore the countryside, with significantly less opportunities to climb stuff, but gives us a pretty cool buggy to drive instead! Running over zombies never gets old, and it's a nice breath of fresh air.

Hellraid is a strange DLC, to say the least. It's a totally separated short story that looks like a Skyrim quest mod more than anything. The "Mostly Negative" reviews for it here on Steam speak for themselves. Terrible DLC, that feels like a boring hack-and-slash fest. Even though this game genre is absolutely amazing, Dying Light does NOT pull it off well. One of the worst DLCs I have ever played, despite having a bit of fun.

There's a Co-Op multiplayer component in Dying Light. Personally, I didn't enjoy it too much, since the game is now pretty much dead. Every player is either AFK on the pause menu and doesn't acknowledge your presence at all, or just runs laps around a safezone, or kicks you instantly. Zombie invasions where people "invade" your lobby and have to attack you while playing as a night hunter is too unbalanced to be fun. The concept sounds great, but once you start getting stomped by players with 3k hours in the game while you want to play the game at your own pace, you'll realize it's poorly executed. Dying Light is best played entirely as a singleplayer experience. Plus, seeing other players ruins the immersion entirely, since the story is about YOU, Kyle Crane, being the best runner in The Tower capable of everything, and having someone else just throws that narrative point right out the window.

When it comes to achievements, it's where the game gets EVEN worse, and it hits the fan... As a committed achievement hunter for 5 years at the writing of this review and 55 finished games on my belt, I declare Dying Light the WORST completion I have ever undergone. The vast majority of them can be obtained solo and pretty easily. Some are extremely difficult to pull off, but doable, shall you put on your try hard shoes. But the ones that require the cooperation of other players towards the same goal, and the ones that directly need RNGesus' blessing are the equivalent of waterboarding torture. Trying to accomplish and/or organize anything with the VERY few people playing a dead multiplayer game is a terrible endeavour, and I'm referring to the "Together Till The End", "Polyamory", "Harran Athletics" and "Lucky 7" achievements. Relying on pure luck and exploits is also an idiotic move from Techland, when it comes to the stupidly named "Homo Homini Lupus Est" achievement, that is IMPOSSIBLE to unlock once you advance enough in the main story, and the only mean to farm for it is by using a famous exploit.

Despite all these negative points I've listed, Dying Light remains one of my favorite games of all time. This game is incredible in what it does well! I expect to put more hours in it in the future, long after reviewing it, since it is permanently up for revisiting for me! Open-World zombie survival-horror with nearly unlimited Parkour... Need I say more? There are very few games that really get this genre down right, but let me just say that Dying Light is definitely one of them. I honestly didn't expect the gameplay to be as good as it was and in spite of having been released almost 6 years ago this game hasn't fallen behind in terms of quality, even by today's standards.

The strongest point about this game for me was, of course, the Parkour. Literally every inch of the map, it's buildings, vehicles and even the zombies themselves are all but stepping stones for you on your quest to find the cure for the virus. The maps are large enough for you to be able to explore for hours, and being able to move around as freely as you are thanks to the parkour really makes this feel less like a chore and more like an obstacle course with an endless amount of routes that you can take to reach your destination.

Combat-wise there are several options that you can play around and experiment with that I think will satisfy pretty much everyone's own personal combat style, and as the sun goes down... well, we all know the night is dark and full of terrors. Some of the strongest enemies in the game like to come out and play at night, and it really does fill you with a sense urgency to get to a safe zone whenever night comes about. This day and night cycle is more then just a game mechanic... it really adds more life to the gameplay.

One other great feature for this game is definitely the Co-op mode. Though you have to get through the prologue in order to be able to play with a friend, and the final story sequences are only playable in single player, Co-op definitely enhances the experience. Not only that, I found the "Be the Zombie" mode to be one of the most intense and exhilarating experiences I've had in a long time. If you have multiplayer enabled then you could be randomly invaded by another player playing as an advanced volatile zombie who's only mission in life is to end yours. This mode definitely favors the zombie but is by no means impossible, and it only gets more exciting if you're playing with a friend with which you can plan out different strategies to beat the zombie. If you prefer to be the one to torture the living though, you can play as the zombie yourself and find different people to invade and torment as you master the arts of the darkness, either way both are extremely fun and worth trying at least once.

One thing that I didn't like so much about the game though was it's story. Don't get me wrong, it's good and all and it serves it's purpose in setting about a narrative for you to play through, but it just didn't cut it for me. I found it didn't make much sense at times, there were many plot holes and characters just felt hollow. You can tell that they tried to make some bits emotional, but it just seemed too forced in the end... I'm probably doing a terrible job at explaining myself here, but all I can say is that the story could have used a bit more work. That being said, the story is probably the last reason why I played this game, and the gameplay is so good that the story is merely but a vessel through which you can experience the game.

All in all Dying Light is a beautifully crafted open-world survival-horror game that is definitely worth your time to check out. Even to this date there are still constant updates and events that help keep the game feeling fresh, the story might not be the best but the gameplay more than makes up for it and you will definitely have more then enough to do here to keep you entertained for hours on end.

[code][i]Dying Light[/i] is an open world first-person survival horror video game developed by Techland and published by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment.[/code]


[h1]👋 First impression[/h1]

Before I entered this game, I thought that this would be another game representing the world in a zombie apocalypse and there would be nothing different in it from the others. When I came in and saw that my character was just parachuting from a plane into an area full of zombies, I realized that the game would be very good.

    [th]❌Cons[/th]

         • An open world to kill as many zombies as you want[/td]
    [td]• Sometimes the game crashes when i Alt + Tab[/td]
  [/tr]
[/table]

[h1]🎮 Gameplay[/h1]

[b]•Combat:[/b]
The gameplay takes place in a city full of zombies named Harran. The battles are mainly in melee range with melee weapons like swords, wrenches, knives, pipes etc. I say mainly because they are not just melee weapons. There are also guns that are used mainly to eliminate bandits, as they block many melee strikes and can take a long time until someone is killed by such a weapon. Some of them even have other rifles.

[b]•Weapons:[/b]
Melee weapons are a lot of fun to use because you can cut off the heads of zombies and see them flying around, and as for guns, they are pretty straight forward. There is no bullet drop, which is normal. I doubt anyone would get into the game and start thinking about bullet drop, i mean this is not Battlefield. Something that impressed me, however, was the bow. Shooting with it can be a little bit weird and take some time to get used to. There's a arrow drop on it. 

[b]•Day and Night:[/b]
Dying Light has day and night and the two are completely different not only because it gets darker or lighter. What distinguishes night from day are Volatiles and the fact that other zombies get damage buffs and can also climb walls like the runners. Players can also use environmental traps, such as spikes and electrified fences to kill the infected. Daytime will last for approximately 64 minutes, while night time will last for approximately 7 minutes.

[b]•Crafting & Blueprints:[/b]
Crafting in this game is something very important. Whether you want to get seriously involved in modifying weapons or you just want to make a simple medkit, you have to craft. You can upgrade your weapons, which increase their stats, make modifications that add some elements to your weapons, such as electricity or poison, or you can make some potions, medkits or lockpicks. 
I told you the sweet tales of crafting, but as you know, if something is too good, then there is a catch. To craft such things, you first need their blueprint. Then you have to gather all the materials that the blueprint wants and then you can craft.

[b]•Level & skills:[/b]
You can raise levels in many different ways. From jumping on buildings to killing zombies. Each level up gives you a skill point that you can use in certain skill trees. There are five perk trees: Survival, Agility, Power, Driver, and Legend.  Survival is your overall skill tree. You will see how to earn points in each category while you play. Just to mention that Driver skill tree is available in [i]The Following DLC.[/i]

[b]•Multiplayer:[/b]
I personally haven't played much online. Only a few times with a friend, but I haven't been to ''Be the Zombie'', for example. Co-op allows a maximum of 4 people to play together, pass quests or make challenges. In "Be the Zombie" you can play as the Night Hunter, which is considered the most evolved type of zombie in [i] Dying Light [/i]. The players who are playing as humans are tasked with destroying the infected nests and surviving attacks performed by the Night Hunter.

[h1]📖 Story[/h1]

[i]Dying Light is an action survival game presented in first-person perspective.[/i] In the story of the game, you play the role of Kyle Crane, an undercover operative who is sent in Harran to find an important file from a rogue political figure. I personally find the story very interesting and obsessive. The game really grabbed my interest and managed to develop some connection between me and the characters  in the story, especially with Jade. (💔)

[h1]🔥 Difficulty[/h1]

At the beginning of the game it is quite difficult because you have almost no weapons, and the ones you have break easily and are weak. However, when you get to the point where you find weapons more often and open enough chests, the game becomes fairly easy at least on normal difficulty. For comparison, I will say that after the normal difficulty there are 2 more difficulties. One is Hard Mode and the other is Nightmare Mode. Things naturally get rough there, in case the game seems too easy for you. I should also mention that playing at night is not easy even on normal difficulty with all these volatiles and I don't even want to imagine what a night run in Nightmare mode is.

[h1]💻 Graphics / Art-style[/h1]

The graphics are beautiful. The zombies are really well made and I just love the animations of killing them. The way the picture slows down to see how you cut off a zombie's head is just an indescribable sight. I should also mention how beautiful it is when, for example, Volatile catches you. It's only beautiful if you watch them catch someone else and not yourself tho.

If you're looking for an exceptional zombie survival experience, Dying Light and its expansion, The Following, are absolute must-plays. The base game masterfully combines fluid, first-person parkour with brutal, satisfying melee combat in the sprawling city of Harran. The dynamic day-night cycle adds incredible tension, as the infected become terrifyingly aggressive after dark.

The Following takes everything that made the original great and expands on it by introducing a massive new countryside map and fully customizable dune buggies, which completely changes how you traverse the world and fight the undead. Whether you're drop-kicking zombies off rooftops in the city or mowing them down in your buggy in the countryside, the gameplay remains endlessly thrilling. Both offer a fantastic co-op experience that only amplifies the fun.


Why Dying Light Shines
* The Parkour System The first-person free-running mechanics are incredibly fluid, allowing you to scale buildings, leap across rooftops, and escape the horde with ease.
* The Day-Night Cycle Daytime lets you scavenge and explore with relative safety, but nightfall brings out the Volatiles—fast, deadly predators that turn the game into a tense survival horror experience.
* Brutal Combat With a deep crafting system, you can create a vast array of modified melee weapons to shock, burn, and bludgeon your way through the infected.


What The Following Adds
* A Massive New Map The expansion moves away from the dense city to a sprawling countryside that is larger than the original game's maps combined.
* Customizable Buggies You get to build and upgrade your own dirt buggy, complete with weapons and unique paint jobs, turning driving into a core part of the gameplay loop.
* A Compelling Narrative It provides a fresh storyline that delves deeper into the mystery of the virus and offers a definitive, unforgettable ending to Kyle Crane's journey.

My relationship with this game is.. complicated. With well over 5000 hours, I can confidently say that the main thing that keeps this game interesting to me is its PvP mode. However, with most devs having been removed from that part of the game for a while, (even before the definitive edition came around) PvP is in a very messy shape.

Story mode isn't a one-and-done campaign. But playing through it about 2-3 times gives you everything it has. The DLCs (The Following, Bozak Horde and Hellraid) keep things interesting for a long while on top of that; but I'm well past that point myself.

Notably, when Definitive came around, Techland decided that adding a bunch of ads for their newer games everywhere was more important than fixing that mess, but you'll see that for yourself. ( The "-nologos" launch command skips the intro, by the way)

On the topic of PvP:
Unpatched modding methods enable some players to crash your game for any and no reason, and even if you don't get crashed or kicked by such a player, the learning curve is steep and unforgiving.

The top tier of PvP is played as essentially an exploit war. For some, like myself, this is a paradise; I dislike how the lack of fixes have led to everyone having cheated weapons and gear, but I -love- having to play this game in the most jank way possible to get an edge; physics bugs like launch glitches, item drop exploits, backward dropkicks. On hunter; Vault tackles, ramp tackles, underwater tackles, drive-by Ground Pounds. (But screw GP-Spit). It's like pitting a group of techhy, sweaty speedrunners together in an arena and telling them "May the jankest tech win".

I wouldn't be playing this game if it weren't as chaotic as it is. But that's also why I cannot recommend this side of the game to anyone who isn't ready for a whooping.

The story and its expansion are a fun experience, but PvP is an unpolished mess; my very best nightmare. Be ready for it, and hopefully, I'll see you there.

The core of the game is solid and fun. The story is interesting even if a bit predictable. The voice acting, sound quality and graphics are all decent.

Where it shines is the parkour and action mechanics. Be very aware however that this is not intended to be a routine first person shooter. If you go into this believing it's a shooter you might be very disappointed. The system is focused very much on running away from the zombies, and when you do engage it will be primarily with melee weapons, weapons that break regularly in order to enforce just how scary the zombies are intended to be and to give you an excuse to craft new and fun little melee weapons.

The majority of the game will be you running and then bashing zombies with a pipe as needed or chopping them to pieces with bladed weapons. Late in the game you do get access to guns, but the noise attracts more zombies and while they are useful tools for certain situations, especially against the occasional human enemies, they are not the focus of the game.

Overall there's easily 40 to 80 hours of fun working your way through the main mission story lines depending on how you approach your choices.

Beyond that, I do have some complaints. There's a lot of "after the story line" content that's been added, particularly with DLC. Much of this feels tacked on, also several components are poorly integrated into the world and are accessible without warning very early despite intending to be end game content. A new player could easily be fooled into wandering into say The Prison or Bozak's Horde without realizing these areas are just completely beyond anything you could attempt at the start of the game. 

There's a lot of "open world fluff" that adds nothing to the experience. Going around collecting silly trophies, pointless racing challenges and various other padding clutter the world just to be treadmills for wasting time. None of this is particularly bad, it just doesn't really improve the core game itself, it's just there as something to do. If you really get into the post-story content and the non-essential challenges, there's theoretically 100's of hours there, but a lot of that is going to be repetitive.

None of that is bad enough to detract from the game since you can easily ignore all of it, or enter a late-game area, die and then just leave and go back to another area, but it can be distracting from what is an otherwise solid game experience.

The main game and story line are totally worth your time to play. The post-story DLC and time wasting challenges will be hit and miss, some people like that stuff, others will skip it.

One final note: Do not buy any of the cosmetic DLC unless you are sure you'll be playing long after the story. You spend the entire game in first person, you don't have any purpose to paying for outfits unless you intend to actually spend a lot of time in post-story coop replaying the same content constantly.

Here's the breakdown of who should dive into Harran and who might want to look elsewhere if you're still on the fence:

[b]Who should play Dying Light:[/b]
[list]
[*]Parkour enthusiasts: If you love the idea of fluid movement and mastering a challenging traversal system, Dying Light's parkour is a major selling point. It's not just a gimmick, it's core to the gameplay and incredibly satisfying to pull off.[*]Zombie fans with a taste for tension: The day/night cycle is a game-changer. If you enjoy the feeling of dread creeping in as the sun sets and the infected become more aggressive, Dying Light delivers that in spades.
[*]Players who like a mix of action and survival: It's not pure survival horror, and it's not just mindless action. Dying Light finds a good balance between scavenging, crafting, combat, and tense escapes.
[*]Those who enjoy open-world exploration: Harran is a big place with lots to discover. If you like exploring and finding hidden secrets, you'll have plenty to do.
[*]Co-op players: Zombie slaying with friends is always a good time, and Dying Light's co-op mode is exceptional between the campaign, challenges, and more. 
[/list]
[b]Who might want to pass on Dying Light:[/b]
[list]
[*]Players who prefer realistic zombie simulations: If you're looking for a game where zombies are slow and easy to dispatch, Dying Light's fast and aggressive infected might not be your cup of tea.
[*]Those who dislike repetition: Mastering the parkour and surviving the night often requires repeating sections. If you get easily frustrated by this, it could be a turn-off.
[*]Players who prioritize story above all else: While the story is decent, it's not the main focus. If you need a strong narrative to stay engaged, you might find it lacking.
[*]Those who are easily scared: The nighttime sequences can be genuinely terrifying. If you're not a fan of jump scares and intense situations, you might find it a bit too much.
[/list]
